deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page, 'Newtons Kegelschnitts Construction'): the ellipse is written in complex form z(u) = m u + n/u with |u| = 1. Its semi-axes are m+n (real) and m−n (imaginary); the axis endpoints are m+n and (m−n)i. The five given points are b = mβ + n/β and likewise c, d, e with parameters γ, δ, ε, normalised so that βγδε = 1. A variable point is p = mερ + n/(ερ). Gauss studies Newton's organic construction. In it one intersection of the rotating legs runs along a straight 'Directrix' while the other traces the conic. On the previous page he had found the directrix point R = f + g(ρ+1)/(ρ−1) and D − b = (m−nγε)(m−nβδ)(m−nδε)/((δ−ε)mn).

Top part: elementary geometry of the conic in this parametrisation. Put u = √(βγ), the 'mid-parameter' of the chord bc.

(1) The chord is b − c = (β−γ)(m − n/(βγ)). Also β − γ = √(βγ)·2i·sin((arg β − arg γ)/2). So b − c is a real multiple of i√(βγ)(m − n/(βγ)) = z(iu). That point lies on the ellipse. Hence it is, in size and position, the semi-diameter parallel to bc. A small 'i' stands before the first formula in the image; it is needed.

(2) The reflection of z(iu) in the major (real) axis is conj(z(iu)) = −i(m/u − nu) = −i(m − βγn)/√(βγ). Gauss writes (m − βγn)/√(βγ) without the factor −i (see errors).

(3) The conjugate semi-diameter of (1) is z(u) = √(βγ)(m + n/(βγ)) = mu + n/u. Gauss deleted an initial 'i' here, correctly.

(4) The tangents at b and c meet at the pole of the chord. The ellipse is the real-linear image w ↦ m w + n w̄ of the unit circle, and the tangents to the circle at β, γ meet at 2βγ/(β+γ). Its image is m·2βγ/(β+γ) + n·2/(β+γ) = (2βγ/(β+γ))(m + n/(βγ)). Equivalently, it is [2√(βγ)/(β+γ)]·z(u), the conjugate semi-diameter stretched by 1/cos((arg β − arg γ)/2). The deleted '2√βγ' fits this second form.

Bottom part: the directrix point t for parameter ρ, quoting 'pag 4 oben':
t = −(m−βδn)(m−γδn)(m−εδn)ρ/(δ(1−ρ)mn) + [(β+γ)m² − mn/ε + δn²]/m.
The leading minus is needed; see errors.

Using βγδε = 1 (so βγδ = 1/ε, γδε = 1/β, βγεδ² = δ), the second part equals b + (γ/m)(m−βδn)(m−εδn). Expanding gives mβ + n/β + γm − n/ε − n/β + δn²/m. By symmetry it also equals c + (β/m)(m−γδn)(m−εδn).

Write γ/m = γδn(1−ρ)/(δ(1−ρ)mn). Then
t = b − [(m−βδn)(m−εδn)/(δ(1−ρ)mn)]·{(m−γδn)ρ − γδn(1−ρ)}.
Since (m−γδn)ρ − γδn(1−ρ) = ρm − γδn, this gives
t = b − (m−βδn)(m−εδn)(ρm−γδn)/(δ(1−ρ)mn).

As ρ runs over the unit circle, (ρm−γδn)/(1−ρ) is a Möbius image of the circle with its pole on the circle. So t runs over a straight line, which is Newton's directrix.

Check (mine): the variable point is at d when ερ = δ, i.e. ρ = δ/ε. There the formula gives t − b = (m−βδn)(m−εδn)(m−γεn)/((δ−ε)mn). This agrees exactly with the previous page's D − b.
errors: Line 2: the reflection of the semi-diameter i√(βγ)(m − n/(βγ)) in the major axis is −i(m − βγn)/√(βγ). Gauss writes (m − βγn)/√(βγ), dropping the factor −i (or an i lost in the writing). As written, the point is generally not on the ellipse.

Tangent point: the image shows a correction/extra '2' before n in (m + 2n/βγ). The correct value is (2βγ/(β+γ))(m + n/(βγ)). With a factor 2 on n the point would be wrong, so the '2' is presumably struck or misread.

Quoted pag-4 formula: the numerator of the second part must be (β+γ)mm − (1/ε)mn + δnn. The term (β+γ)mn read by the machine is incorrect, since only mm makes the identity '= b + (γ/m)(m−βδn)(m−εδn)' hold.

Sign: Gauss's next step and his final result require the first term of t to enter with a minus sign (equivalently ρ/(ρ−1)). With a plus sign the bracket would be ρm + γδn − 2ργδn, not ρm − γδn. The final formula agrees with the previous page's D − b only with the minus. So the mark after 't' is to be read as '= −', and the derivation is then correct.

results.what: Complex parametrisation z = m u + n/u (|u|=1) of an ellipse, with semi-diameter parallel to a chord, its mirror image, and its conjugate expressed through √(βγ).
results.modern_name: Ellipse as affine image of the unit circle, z = a e^{iθ} + b e^{−iθ}; conjugate diameters
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Apollonius for conjugate diameters); complex form standard in 19th c.

results.what: Intersection of the tangents at b, c: (2βγ/(β+γ))(m + n/(βγ)).
results.modern_name: Pole of a chord / tangent intersection on an ellipse

results.what: Closed form of the point on the directrix line in Newton's organic construction of a conic through five points: t = b − (m−βδn)(m−εδn)(ρm−γδn)/(δ(1−ρ)mn).
results.modern_name: Newton's organic (Maclaurin–Braikenridge) construction of a conic through five points, in complex coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (Principia, Book I, Lemma 21 / Arithmetica Universalis); Maclaurin, Braikenridge

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful complex-number computations analysing Newton's classical construction of a conic through five points: conjugate diameters, the pole of a chord, and the directrix line. They are elegant and characteristic of Gauss's complex-variable style, but contain no new theorem.

transcription_corrections: The parameter letters are Greek β (written like a b), γ, δ, ε, as on the previous page.
The first formula carries a leading small 'i': i√(βγ)(m − n/(βγ)). In the third formula the leading 'i' is struck out.
Tangent point: deleted '2√βγ' in the numerator, kept '2βγ/(β+γ)'. The '2' before n in (m + 2n/βγ) appears to be a correction; the mathematically correct form is (m + n/(βγ)).
In the quoted pag-4 formula, the second numerator should read (β+γ)mm − (1/ε)mn + δnn, not (β+γ)mn.
After 't' the mark is a corrected '=' followed by a minus sign ('t = −'), as required by the subsequent derivation.
't = [-…-] b' is a struck character (probably a first 'b' or 'c') followed by b.
